newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Oct 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Oct 15.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

According to research carried out by analysts Mintel, and sponsored by financial adviser lobby group IFAP, an astounding 77 billion stg of ordinary people's money lies unclaimed in Britain's financial institutions. A huge 41 billion stg is stashed and forgotten at banks and building societies alone.

General Motors has charged its former head of purchasing, Jose Ignacio Lopez de Arriortua, now Managing Director at Volkswagen, VW chairman Ferdinand Piech and seven other former GM employees with racketeering, fraud, copyright infringement and theft in connection with his sudden departure from the company on 15 March 1995. GM may seek up to $1 billion (633 million stg) in damages.
ERNST & YOUNG SET TO DISCLOSE PROFITS

Ernst & Young is to reveal its bottom line profits for the first time later this year, following KPMG's earlier move. The other four of the Big Six accountancy firms will continue to keep their financial information a secret. As Ernst has a proportionately larger payroll than KPMG its profits are expected to be significantly lower than KPMG's reported 17.6 million stg for the year to 30 September 1995.
EMU DOUBTS KEEP POUND TOP OF THE POPS
Concern about the prospects for European monetary union is maintaining the popularity of the pound, as Britain is seen as unlikely to be among the first group of states to enter a single currency.
